purpose: This medication helps relieve chest congestion and cough caused by colds, the flu, or other breathing illnesses. It works to loosen mucus in your chest so it is easier to cough up, while also calming your cough reflex. It is specially formulated without sugar, making it a safer choice for people with diabetes.
how_it_works: Guaifenesin, the expectorant part, helps thin and loosen the mucus stuck in your chest and airways so your body can clear it out more easily when you cough. Dextromethorphan, the cough suppressant part, works on the part of your brain that triggers the cough reflex, helping to reduce how often and how hard you cough. Together, they help you feel more comfortable while your body fights off the illness.
common_side_effects: Some people may feel a little dizzy, drowsy, or have an upset stomach, nausea, or vomiting. You might also feel slightly lightheaded. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you are taking antidepressants called MAO inhibitors, as this can cause a serious reaction. Avoid taking more than directed, as too much dextromethorphan can be harmful. Talk to your doctor before using this if you have a chronic cough from smoking, asthma, or other lung conditions. Since it is sugar-free, it is safer for diabetics, but always check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure.
typical_dosing: Follow the directions on the package or as your doctor tells you. Typically, adults take the recommended dose every 4 to 6 hours as needed, and you should not take more than 4 doses in 24 hours. Always use the measuring device included with the medication and drink plenty of water to help loosen mucus.
